chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of our companions, raising it, said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Bashfulness is of two types: bashfulness of intellect and bashfulness of foolishness. So the bashfulness of the intellect is knowledge, and the bashfulness of foolishness is ignorance.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between bashfulness of intellect and bashfulness of foolishness in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith to clarify that modesty is not merely a social virtue but a cognitive indicator, distinguishing between the intellectual restraint that fosters learning and the foolish inhibition that breeds ignorance. This dichotomy reflects the Shia emphasis on 'hayā' as a dynamic force for spiritual and intellectual growth, where true modesty compels one to seek knowledge rather than remain in complacent ignorance. The narration thus redefines modesty as an active engagement with truth, aligning with the broader ethical framework of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of our companions, raising it,

‘Heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The Hiyā (bashfulness) is of two (types) – The Hiyā of the intellect and the Hiyā of foolishness. So the Hiyā of the intellect, it is the knowledge, and the Hiyā of the foolishness, it is the ignorance’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from certain individuals of our people in a marfu’ manner from the Messenger of Allah who has said the following: “

There are two kinds of bashfulness: A bashfulness that comes from one’s reason and the bashfulness that comes from one’s foolishness. The bashfulness that comes from one’s reason is knowledge and the bashfulness that comes from one’s foolishness is ignorance.”
